transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE); Tara Singh (Lumen Tech - Head of ML); Ethan Park (Lumen Tech - Infra Lead); Lydia Gomez (Lumen Tech - Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - quick intro, I'm Maya with Redwood, Rafael is our solutions engineer, hi Rafael.
[00:06] Rafael: Hey, hi all. Good to see you. Sorry for the slight delay on my end, had a calendar overlap.
[00:11] Tara: No worries, thanks for setting this up, Maya. We wanted to focus today on renewal timing and expansion - specifically EU-west and burst capacity for holiday traffic.
[00:21] Maya: Yep, that's the goal. Just to confirm agenda - renewal terms, committed capacity vs burst, region expansion, and then any security/procurement asks. Sound good?
[00:28] Ethan: Sounds good. We also want to talk about a couple of latency incidents from last month, p95 spikes around a large batch job.
[00:35] Lydia: And procurement timeline - FYI we have a PO window mid-September.

[02:10] Rafael: Quick context from our side: Lumen is on our Hosted plan today with about 250M tokens/month and a small Dedicated pool for inference experiments. The renewal that kicks in October has some flexibility - if you commit to a Reserved Dedicated plan we can guarantee throughput and lower unit cost. There are a few approaches: 1) Increase hosted tier and add region egress, 2) Move to Dedicated for predictable latency, or 3) Hybrid with routing for cost-control.
[03:00] Tara: For latency - our main apps are user-facing chat (low-latency requirement p95 < 450ms) and nightly scoring batch jobs where latency is less critical but throughput matters. The p95 spikes hit 700-900ms once during the last batch window.
[03:18] Rafael: Got it. That aligns with what we saw - batch jobs sometimes contend for KV cache resources. One option is to isolate batch traffic to separate Dedicated nodes or use a dedicated routing tag to ensure it doesn't evict hot prefix caches for chat.
[04:05] Ethan: Can you give ballpark numbers for Dedicated sizing? We ran a rough estimate but would like Redwood's recommendation for 99th percentile and for concurrency.
[04:15] Rafael: Sure - for your current model mix (mix of 13B and 70B open models) and expected burst concurrency of ~120 qps during peak, we'd recommend a Dedicated pool of 8x A10g-equivalent for baseline with ability to burst to 12x for holidays. That gives headroom for p95 targets. I'll share exact throughput calc in the follow-up doc.
[05:05] Tara: 8x A10g-equivalent - okay. Any options for EU-west? We need data residency plus lower latency for EU users.
[05:15] Maya: We can provision Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 as part of Dedicated or Private deployments. Cost differs a bit by region. For Hosted, we have a managed multi-region offering - but cross-region egress applies. Rafael will include region delta pricing.

[07:00] Lydia: On procurement, if we commit to 12 months do we get deeper discounts? And what about contract amendment lead time?
[07:10] Maya: Yes, annual reserved capacity gives better unit pricing and priority capacity. Lead time for an amendment is typically 2-3 weeks for signature and procurement admin - we can align timing to your mid-September PO window.
[07:22] Lydia: Good, thanks.

[09:10] Ethan: About the p95 spikes - is there a recommended quick mitigation we can do while we decide on Dedicated? We'd like something low-effort.
[09:20] Rafael: A few quick mitigations: 1) Enable request-level routing to separate batch traffic, 2) Prefix-level KV cache pinning for hot sessions, 3) Short-term autoscaling knobs to raise concurrency limits during the nightly window. These are config changes; we can push suggested defaults. There may be slight cost bump but minimal engineering work.
[10:05] Tara: Request routing - is that available on Hosted or only Dedicated?
[10:12] Rafael: It's available on Hosted as part of the traffic routing rules; you can define route by tag or path and set priority. Dedicated gives more isolation but Hosted routing is a good interim step.

[12:00] Maya: On security/compliance ask - last time you asked for audit logs and SAML logs - anything new?
[12:08] Tara: We want to confirm KMS integration for key material and whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM in eu-west region. Also SOC2 attestation copy for the renewal pack.
[12:22] Maya: We have KMS options (Cloud KMS + HSM for Private). For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; forwarding logs to your SIEM is supported. I'll attach the SOC2 cert and security pack in the follow-up.

[14:30] Ethan: Any caveats on cross-region failover? If eu-west goes down, can traffic failover to us-east with minimal latency penalty?
[14:40] Rafael: Yes, we support policy-based failover. For production-grade failover we recommend Active-Passive with warmed standby in failover region to avoid cold-start issues. Cost is higher for warm standby but recovery is faster.

[17:10] Tara: Pricing - can you show an example with current tokens, 12-month commit, and EU region added?
[17:20] Maya: We'll send a table: current usage, projected tokens for next 12 months, pricing tiers for Hosted vs Dedicated, and committed capacity options. We'll include a side-by-side cost per 1M tokens including region deltas and burst costs.
[18:05] Lydia: Also please note our procurement prefers line items for decimalized pricing - we need monthly invoices.
[18:12] Maya: Noted; we'll include monthly invoice breakdown.

[20:00] Rafael: Quick technical note - for the 70B model we recommend using INT8 quantization in Dedicated to reduce GPU memory footprint; sometimes that reduces p95 by 50-100ms for generation-heavy workloads. We'll include quantization profile recommendations and any quality tradeoffs.
[20:20] Tara: Did you see any quality regressions with quantization in previous tests?
[20:25] Rafael: Minor in some prompt types, but for chat flows with constrained prompts it's minimal. We'll share a short evaluation report.

[22:30] Ethan: For the bench that you're going to run - can we provide a sample dataset and expected SLOs so results match our traffic?
[22:38] Rafael: Absolutely, please send a representative prompt set and we'd run bench with your requested concurrency and token mix.
[23:00] Tara: We'll share two weeks worth of anonymized logs for sampling.

[25:10] Maya: TL;DR on our action items: Maya will send pricing and renewal options; Rafael will run throughput and quantization bench; Ethan will give traffic SLOs and logs; Lydia will confirm procurement timeline. Any additions?
[25:28] Lydia: That covers it.

[28:05] Rafael: One more note on routing policies - you can do percentage-based routing to migrate gradually to Dedicated or new region - useful during cutover to avoid big surges.
[28:20] Tara: That's helpful.

[31:00] Ethan: On SLAs, what uptime guarantees for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[31:08] Maya: Dedicated offers SLA-backed uptime and latency targets specific to the pool; Hosted has best-effort with prioritized support tiers - for enterprise customers we can include an SLA addendum.
[31:28] Lydia: Would an SLA addendum delay procurement? Our security team needs legal to review.
[31:35] Maya: We can provide standard SLA addendum template for your legal; Rafael can loop legal as needed.

[34:00] Tara: Anything else on multi-region data residency? We need assurance that EU data stays in EU region for storage and logs.
[34:10] Maya: For Dedicated in EU, data at rest and logs can be kept in region. For Hosted, we can configure EU tenancy and KMS in your region; we'll document the configuration steps.

[37:05] Rafael: To confirm next steps on the bench: if you send logs by Monday (2026-08-17) we'll aim to run bench and share results by Wednesday (2026-08-19).
[37:20] Ethan: That works.

[39:40] Maya: Recap - We'll send: pricing table and region delta (Maya), throughput calc and bench runs + quantization notes (Rafael), Lumen sends logs/SLOs (Ethan), procurement timeline confirmation (Lydia). Tentative follow up meeting to review bench results: Friday 2026-08-21 at 16:00 UTC. Does that work?
[39:55] Tara: Yes.
[40:00] Lydia: Works for procurement.

[42:15] Maya: Anything else? If not we'll close.
[42:20] Tara: One tiny ask - can you include a sample runbook for failover steps? Our SRE would like an ops checklist.
[42:28] Rafael: Yep, we'll attach an ops checklist and failover playbook.
[42:35] Maya: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the items.
[42:42] Ethan: Thanks all.
[42:45] Meeting ended.
